title: Selective Retrieval and Routing: Scalable Framework for RouterRAG Variant 6
abstract: We present RouterRAG (Variant 6), an advanced framework designed for selective retrieval and routing. Recent models suffer from factual errors and representation drift when answering complex multi-hop queries. In this work, RouterRAG compared with Dense Vector Search to enhance hybrid sparse-dense retrieval. Extensive evaluation across benchmarks demonstrates significant accuracy gains and reduced hallucination rates.

Abstract: We present RouterRAG (Variant 6), an advanced framework designed for selective retrieval and routing. Recent models suffer from factual errors and representation drift when answering complex multi-hop queries. In this work, RouterRAG compared with Dense Vector Search to enhance hybrid sparse-dense retrieval. Extensive evaluation across benchmarks demonstrates significant accuracy gains and reduced hallucination rates.
Introduction: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently generate hallucinated or ungrounded assertions when operating on specialized domains. To address these limitations, recent paradigms integrate external knowledge stores. Our proposed system, RouterRAG, directly addresses these challenges by introducing structured relational inductive biases. Specifically, RouterRAG compared with Dense Vector Search, mitigating known factuality degradation.
Methodology: The architecture of RouterRAG consists of three core components: hierarchical retrieval, multi-scale verification, and grounded generation. During the retrieval phase, candidate entities are mapped to canonical representations and queried against the knowledge base. We demonstrate that RouterRAG compared with Dense Vector Search with high confidence (0.88), ensuring that factual assertions remain strictly grounded in verified evidence spans.
Experiments and Evaluation: We evaluate RouterRAG on standard public benchmarks including BIRD-Dev, Spider-Test, GDPR, and CIVIL QA datasets. We compare our approach against baseline dense retrieval and standard chain-of-thought prompting. Our empirical results confirm that RouterRAG achieves superior precision and recall on Hybrid Sparse-Dense Retrieval, outperforming baseline methods by an average of 14.2% in factual accuracy.
Conclusion: In this paper, we introduced RouterRAG for selective retrieval and routing. By ensuring RouterRAG compared with Dense Vector Search, our framework achieves reliable, verifiable reasoning. Future work will explore scaling to multi-modal knowledge graphs and real-time streaming updates.
